To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

total serum antioxidant capacity (TAS) was lower in men with coronary artery disease (CAD) compared with healthy controls, but the difference disappeared after adjustment for the confounders, and uric acid, triglycerides, systolic blood pressure, current smoking, and glucose levels contributed to TAS variance.

the main independent determinants of total serum antioxidant capacity (TASC) are uric acid, triglycerides, systolic blood pressure and current smoking, while presence of coronary heart disease itself is not an independent determinant of TAC.
in men with and without CHD, the total antioxidant capacity of blood serum was mainly determined by serum uric acid concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the issue of whether CHD is related to a decline in total antioxidant capacity.
the role of TAC of serum in CHD and its relationship to the metabolic syndrome.
the relationship between TAC of blood and cardiovascular risk factors in men.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TAC is a complex parameter that reflects the overall antioxidant defense status and that is related to several factors that may contribute to the pathogenesis of CHD.
the TAC level is a marker of the risk of CHD, rather than an independent determinant.
the TAC of blood is a marker of metabolic syndrome, not of CHD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in men with CHD the TAC level is not lower than in age-matched peers, and the observed differences in TAC levels between the groups are not independent predictors of the presence of CHD.
TAC of blood is a marker of metabolic syndrome rather than of CHD itself.
the higher TAC observed in patients with CHDC could be due to higher UA concentrations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TAC may be a useful biomarker of CHD, although its role in the development of CHD is still unclear.
the TAC of blood may serve as an additional marker for the metabolic syndrome and may be a useful indicator of CHD risk in men.
the antioxidant capacity of the body may be influenced by several factors, including lifestyle and metabolic status.
